rows.title: Filing of announcements in XBRL format on NSE Electronic Application Processing System (NEAPS) platform
rows.summary:
NSE has announced that, starting **January 28, 2023**, listed companies must begin filing certain disclosures on the **NEAPS platform in XBRL format**, alongside the existing PDF filing requirement under **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**. The XBRL filing facility applies to **Regulation 29** disclosures for **prior intimation of a Board meeting** and to specific **Regulation 30** disclosures, namely: **changes in directors or key managerial personnel** (including Managing Director, CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, etc.), **auditor**, **compliance officer**, and **share transfer agent**; **outcomes of Board meetings** relating to **dividend, buyback, bonus issue, or voluntary delisting**; and announcements regarding **acquisition(s)** (including agreements to acquire), **schemes of arrangement** such as **amalgamation, merger, demerger, restructuring**, or the **sale/disposal of any unit, division, subsidiary, or other restructuring**.

Until further notice, listed entities must continue to make the disclosure in **PDF mode** as currently required under Regulation 30, and then file the corresponding **XBRL version within 24 hours of the PDF submission**. The circular also states that NSE will **later transition to XBRL-only submission**, but the **date has not yet been announced** and will be communicated separately. Compliance teams should therefore ensure their internal process captures both filings for the covered announcement types, with the XBRL follow-up deadline tracked as **24 hours after the PDF filing**.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
This circular is addressed to all listed entities and reiterates their obligation under Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 to maintain a Structured Digital Database (“SDD”). It refers back to earlier NSE circulars that set timelines for filing the SDD compliance certificate for the quarters ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022, and another circular that described the consequences for non-compliance with the SDD requirements.

The key compliance consequence highlighted here is that if a listed company is found non-compliant with Regulation 3(5) or 3(6), the Exchange will display a non-compliance status on the company’s “Get Quote” page on the Exchange website starting from the next trading day, and that status will remain visible until the Exchange is satisfied that the company has fully complied. The circular further clarifies that the compliance officer’s details will also be displayed on the same page alongside the non-compliance information. This makes the SDD obligation not just an internal recordkeeping requirement but a publicly visible compliance issue with immediate market-facing consequences.

The circular also states that it supersedes the earlier NSE circular referenced as NSE/CML/2023/09 dated January 25, 2023. Listed companies are therefore expected to take note of this updated position, ensure continued compliance with SDD maintenance and certification requirements, and be aware that non-compliance may be publicly disclosed through the Exchange website with the compliance officer’s details attached.

rows.title: Standard Operating Process under SEBI(PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (“SDD”)
rows.summary:
This notice reiterates that under Regulations 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, listed companies must maintain a Structured Digital Database (“SDD”), and it builds on earlier NSE circulars: NSE/CML/2022/51 dated October 28, 2022, which set timelines for submitting the SDD compliance certificate for the quarters ended September 30, 2022 and December 31, 2022, and NSE/CML/2022/52 dated November 4, 2022, which set out consequences for non-compliance with those SDD requirements. The new clarification is that for listed entities subject to Regulation 24A of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, the Secretarial Auditor must specifically confirm compliance with the SDD requirement in the Annual Secretarial Audit Report, and listed companies are instructed to ensure their Secretarial Auditor is informed of this obligation. The notice also reinforces the enforcement consequence for non-compliance: the Exchange will display on the listed entity’s “Get Quote” page that the company is non-compliant with SDD starting from the next trading day, and this display will continue until the Exchange has satisfactorily verified that the company has fully complied.

In addition to the website disclosure, the notice states that the name of the compliance officer will also be published in the Exchange’s records/communication in the context of non-compliance, indicating that responsibility is not limited to the entity itself. The practical compliance implication is that listed entities must ensure their SDD is properly maintained, compliance evidence is available for periodic certification, and Secretarial Audit processes are aligned so that SDD compliance is explicitly tested and reported where Regulation 24A applies. The notice does not change the underlying SDD maintenance requirement itself, but it heightens the audit and disclosure consequences for failures and makes clear that non-compliance will be visible to the market until remedied and verified by the Exchange.

rows.title: Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means
rows.summary: This NSE circular (NSE/CML/2023/08 dated 13 January 2023) is an information/transmission notice to all listed companies, specifically forwarding SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div2/P/CIR/2023/13 dated 12 January 2023 on the “Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of REITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means.” The NSE states that a copy of the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website, and asks recipients to take necessary action at their end. The document itself does not set out the substantive meeting procedure, voting rules, thresholds, or deadlines; it merely alerts addressees that SEBI has issued guidance permitting or governing REIT unit-holder meetings via video conferencing or other audio-visual means. For compliance purposes, the key point is that entities responsible for REIT-related governance should review the attached SEBI circular and implement any required meeting-conduct procedures in line with that SEBI direction.

rows.title: Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of InvITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) issued Circular No. **NSE/CML/2023/07** on **13 January 2023** to inform listed companies of a SEBI circular dated **12 January 2023** titled **“Facility of conducting meetings of unit holders of InvITs through Video Conferencing or Other Audio-Visual means.”** The NSE notice itself does not set out the detailed compliance requirements; rather, it alerts recipients that SEBI has issued the referenced circular and says a copy is enclosed and available on the NSE website for necessary action.

For a compliance team, the practical point is that this communication is directed to **listed companies** and concerns the **conduct of meetings of unitholders of Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs)** through **video conferencing or other audio-visual means**. The NSE letter does not specify implementation mechanics, voting procedures, quorum rules, deadlines, or thresholds; those details would be in the underlying SEBI circular dated 12 January 2023, which this notice incorporates by reference. Compliance should therefore review the SEBI circular directly to determine the exact obligations, affected entities, and any operational requirements for convening InvIT unitholder meetings electronically.

rows.title: Circular for seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to Corporate Debt Restructuring
rows.summary:
This circular, dated **January 11, 2023** and issued by the **NSE Listing/Capital Markets Department**, is a **request for comments/feedback** on a proposal to move **announcements relating to Corporate Debt Restructuring (CDR)** from the current **PDF submission format to exclusive XBRL submission**. It states that this change would be made under the framework of **SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (LODR)**, read with the **SEBI Circular dated September 9, 2015**, as amended, and any other applicable law.

The document explains that listed entities already have to make periodic and event-based compliance filings to stock exchanges within prescribed timelines, and that **XBRL reporting has been in place for financial filings since 2015**. NSE says stock exchanges have been progressively converting other SEBI-regulated filings from PDF to XBRL to standardize securities-market data, create consistent data structures, reduce compliance burden for listed entities, and make the data easier to analyze. The specific filing being targeted here is **corporate announcements pertaining to Corporate Debt Restructuring**, which, if the proposal proceeds, would need to be filed **only in XBRL format** rather than PDF.

For compliance teams, the practical implication is that **all listed entities subject to LODR disclosure requirements for CDR announcements** should review the proposed migration and be prepared for a future obligation to use the **XBRL templates/formats that NSE says will be provided in paragraph 4** of the full circular. The circular itself is **not yet a final operative rule** imposing a new filing obligation; rather, it is seeking stakeholder feedback on the proposal. The document does not specify a final implementation date, transition period, threshold, or penalty in the text provided, but it clearly signals the direction of travel: **CDR-related announcements are intended to become XBRL-only compliance filings** once implemented.

rows.title: Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a notice to all members that SEBI issued a new circular on January 10, 2023 titled “Comprehensive Framework on Offer for Sale (OFS) of Shares through Stock Exchange Mechanism.” The NSE document itself does not set out the substantive OFS rules; it simply transmits SEBI’s circular for reference and “necessary action” by recipients, and says the SEBI circular is enclosed and also available on the NSE website.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the document confirms a regulatory update affecting the stock-exchange mechanism for Offer for Sale transactions in India, but it does not specify the detailed changes, thresholds, procedures, or deadlines in the text provided here. The NSE circular is dated January 11, 2023 and is addressed to all members, meaning any NSE member involved in OFS activity should review and implement the underlying SEBI circular dated January 10, 2023. No separate implementation date, transition period, pricing rule, allocation threshold, or procedural requirement is stated in the NSE covering note itself.

rows.title: Circular for seeking comments, feedback from Listed Entities for XBRL being introduce for  submission of Announcements pertaining to all Notices of Shareholders Meeting in phase manner
rows.summary:
NSE’s Listing Department circular dated January 10, 2023 (Ref. NSE/CML/2023/04) is a consultation document seeking comments and feedback from all listed companies on a proposed migration from PDF to XBRL for corporate announcements relating to all notices of shareholders’ meetings. The proposal is being introduced in phases and is intended to standardize disclosure data for market use, while aligning with the disclosure obligations under SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 and the SEBI circular dated September 9, 2015, as amended.

The circular explains that listed entities already file periodic compliance information and that XBRL has been mandated for financial filings since 2015; stock exchanges are now extending that approach to other Regulation 30 disclosures, including shareholder-meeting notices. Under the proposal, announcements pertaining to all notices of shareholders’ meetings would need to be filed exclusively in XBRL format, replacing PDF for those submissions once the phased implementation is in effect. The stated purpose is to create identical, homogeneous data structures across filings, which the exchange says should reduce compliance burden for listed entities and make the reported data easier to analyze.

For compliance teams, the practical implication is that this is not yet a final operational instruction in the text provided, but a request for feedback on the move to mandatory XBRL-based submission for these notices. The document does not provide the full phased timetable in the excerpt, but it clearly signals that listed entities should prepare for XBRL-only filing requirements for shareholder meeting notices as part of the broader transition away from PDF-based disclosures.

rows.title: Filing of SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 disclosure to Exchange
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India has changed the filing route for disclosures made under the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011. Effective **January 7, 2023**, all such SEBI SAST disclosures must be filed through the Exchange’s dedicated **Takeover email ID: takeover@nse.co.in**, rather than through the earlier filing arrangement referenced in the prior circulars about the New Digital Portal. This circular is a continuation of **NSE/CML/2022/03 dated January 6, 2022** and **NSE/CML/2022/09 dated February 17, 2022**, which had informed members about the launch of the new digital portal for Exchange filings.

For compliance purposes, companies and other filing entities subject to SEBI SAST disclosure obligations need to ensure that any required takeover-related disclosures are sent to the specified email address from the effective date onward. The circular does not change the underlying SEBI SAST disclosure requirements themselves; it changes the **submission channel** for filings with the Exchange. The Exchange also notes that its officer contact details are available on the **NEAPS portal**, and companies may contact the relevant officers there for questions or filing issues related to SEBI SAST disclosures.

rows.title: Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 –Reg.
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated 06 January 2023, is a forwarding notice to **all listed companies** and their Company Secretaries, informing them of a corresponding **SEBI circular dated 05 January 2023** titled **“Relaxation from compliance with certain provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Reg.”** The NSE communication itself does **not** set out the underlying relaxation terms, amended obligations, or any new compliance deadlines; it simply states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be acted upon as necessary.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that the change comes from **SEBI’s circular of 05 January 2023**, and the NSE is directing listed entities to review that circular for the actual relief granted from certain **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015** requirements. The notice indicates that the circular is available on the NSE website as well, and it is issued as an informational transmission from the National Stock Exchange of India Ltd., signed by **Sandeep Dhamal, Manager**. Because the content provided does not specify which provisions were relaxed, which entities are exempted, or any effective period beyond the SEBI circular date, a compliance officer would need to consult the attached SEBI circular itself to determine the exact reporting, disclosure, or procedural changes applicable to their listed entity.

rows.title: Circular for seeking comments, feedback from Listed Entities for XBRL being introduce for issuance of securities, alteration of capital, action which will result in alteration of the terms or structure of any existing securities, any restriction on transferability of securities or forfeiture of securities, alteration, any restriction on transferability of securities.
rows.summary:
This circular from NSE’s Listing Department (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2023/01, dated January 5, 2023) is a consultation notice to all listed companies seeking comments and feedback on a proposal to move certain corporate announcements from PDF format to XBRL format. The stated purpose is to standardize securities-market data and expand the existing XBRL reporting framework beyond financial filings to cover corporate disclosures made under SEBI’s Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015 (LODR), read together with the SEBI circular dated September 9, 2015, as amended.

The change would affect announcements relating to issuance or forfeiture of securities, split or consolidation of shares, any restriction on transferability of securities, and alterations in the terms or structure of existing securities. The document specifically references actions such as forfeiture and reissue of forfeited securities, alteration of calls, and redemption of securities, indicating that both the original corporate action and any subsequent changes to the terms/structure of securities are intended to be captured in XBRL. In practical terms, listed entities that currently submit these announcements in PDF would, if the proposal is implemented, need to transition to XBRL-based submission for these disclosure categories.

The circular also notes the regulatory context: listed entities already have obligations to submit periodic compliance filings within prescribed timelines under SEBI Listing Regulations, and XBRL has already been mandated for financial filings since 2015. Stock exchanges have been progressively converting other filings under SEBI regulations from PDF to XBRL, and this proposal is presented as the next step in that phased migration. No operative compliance deadline, effective date, or final implementation timeline is stated in the provided text; the immediate action requested is stakeholder feedback/comments on the proposal before any formal rollout.

rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 and 59A of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements.
rows.summary:
This circular revises the Standard Operating Procedure for listed entities filing a draft Scheme of Arrangement with stock exchanges under Regulation 37 and Regulation 59A of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. For compliance purposes, the key change is that the scheme seeking the exchange’s no-objection certificate must be submitted **within 15 working days of the board meeting** approving the draft scheme, together with **all documents required under the Exchange checklist**. If the application is **not filed within that 15-working-day window**, the company cannot rely on the earlier board approval and must obtain **fresh board approval** based on updated materials, specifically including **fresh financials, a new valuation report, and similar current information**.

At the time of filing under Regulations 37 and 59A, the listed entity must also submit the **audited financial statements of the last 3 years** for any **unlisted company(ies) involved in the scheme**. These financials must be **not older than 6 months**, and this requirement is stated to be in line with the referenced SEBI circulars and master circulars, including the March 10, 2017 SEBI circular and the November 17, 2022 SEBI circular. The document makes clear that these audited financials are a mandatory part of the exchange review package and are to be considered for processing the scheme application.

The circular applies to **all listed companies** and is issued by NSE’s Listing department under reference **NSE/CML/2022/61 dated December 20, 2022**. The compliance implication is that listed entities planning a scheme of arrangement must tightly coordinate board approval timing, filing timing, and supporting financial documentation so that the submission stays within the 15-working-day limit and remains supported by current financial/valuation evidence.

rows.title: Clarifications with respect to SEBI Circular no. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHSRACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022 (“SEBI Circular”), on Scheme(s) of Arrangement by entities who have listed their Non-convertible Debt securities (NCDs)/ Non-convertible Redeemable Preference shares (NCRPS)’
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, issued on December 19, 2022, provides implementation clarifications for SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS-RACPOD1/P/CIR/2022/156 dated November 17, 2022, which sets out the procedure for schemes of arrangement by listed entities that have listed non-convertible debt securities (NCDs) and/or non-convertible redeemable preference shares (NCRPS). The circular clarifies that the amended requirements apply only where the board meeting approving the scheme of arrangement was held after November 14, 2022, which is the date the relevant amendments to the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 took effect.

A key compliance obligation concerns the report on complaints/comments received on the draft scheme. Where a listed entity has both specified securities and NCDs/NCRPS listed, it must submit the complaints report to the stock exchanges within 7 days after the expiry of a 21-day period from the date the draft scheme is hosted on the stock exchanges’ websites and the listed entity’s website. Where the listed entity has only NCDs/NCRPS listed, the complaints report must be submitted within 7 days after the expiry of a 10-day period from the date the draft scheme is hosted on the stock exchanges’ websites and the listed entity’s website. In both cases, the draft scheme and related documents must be hosted on the stock exchanges’ and the listed entity’s websites.

The circular also indicates that further timelines are being addressed for processing the scheme under the SEBI framework, so compliance teams should align internal review, board approval, disclosure, and filing workflows to the post-November 14, 2022 applicability date and the specific 10-day or 21-day public-comment periods, followed by the 7-day filing deadline for the complaints report. Entities with listed NCDs/NCRPS should determine whether they fall into the “specified securities plus NCDs/NCRPS” category or the “only NCDs/NCRPS” category, because the public consultation period and subsequent reporting deadline differ depending on the listing structure.

rows.title: Circular pertaining to submission of the Aadhar details in the Announcement/Offer Documents submitted to the Exchange.
rows.summary:
The Exchange is instructing all listed entities and all issuers proposing to list securities not to publicly disclose Aadhaar numbers, Aadhaar cards, Aadhaar-related demographic information, or photographs in announcements or offer-related documents, in line with Section 29(4) of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 as amended in 2019. The circular emphasizes that where an organization’s governing law requires Aadhaar information to be published, it must be published only in masked form, not as full unmasked details.

For listed entities making announcements, the Exchange has specifically observed that some are uploading newspaper clippings that contain Aadhaar numbers or other unrelated content on the same page. The required change is that the entity should submit only the clipping pertaining to its own announcement and must not upload the entire newspaper page if it includes other material, especially any Aadhaar-related details.

For companies and issuers submitting draft offer documents or offer documents to the Exchange, Aadhaar numbers and related information of promoters or other persons required under applicable SEBI regulations, including the SEBI (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2018 and the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Non-Convertible Securities) Regulations, 2021, must not appear in the public draft/offer document or any other public document. Instead, those Aadhaar details must be provided to the Exchange separately through a non-public channel or separate submission. The practical compliance obligation is to remove or mask Aadhaar data from all public-facing filings and ensure internal filing procedures distinguish between documents submitted publicly and Aadhaar information submitted separately to the Exchange.

The circular is dated December 19, 2022 and applies immediately to all listed entities and all entities/issuers that intend to list securities with the Exchange.

rows.title: Circular for filing of Equity announcements and Financial Results to be made available on the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) platform
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) has directed all listed companies that, starting **December 17, 2022**, filings for **Equity Announcements and Financial Results** must be made **only through the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System) portal**. This change is part of the Exchange’s effort to consolidate filings into a **single portal**, following earlier circulars dated **January 6, 2022**, **February 17, 2022**, and **July 8, 2022** relating to the launch of the new digital filing system.

For compliance purposes, companies must continue filing these disclosures in the **same NEAPS manner that was available in February 2022**, but now exclusively through NEAPS for the covered subjects. The circular clarifies the filing route based on the type of board meeting outcome: if the board meeting has **only financial results** as the agenda item, the **quarterly, half-yearly, or annual financial results PDF** must be filed **only under the “Quick Results” module** on NEAPS. If the board meeting has **multiple agenda items including financial results**, the disclosure must be filed under **both the “Announcement” module and the “Quick Results” module** on NEAPS. In addition, the **XBRL submission** for financial results must be filed under the **“Full Results” module** on NEAPS.

The circular also notes that **Exchange officer contact details for each subject are available on the NEAPS portal**, and companies should use those contacts for issues or queries related to filings on the platform. The notice is addressed to **all listed companies**, so any issuer subject to NSE listing obligations must ensure internal filing procedures are updated to reflect the mandatory NEAPS-only workflow from the effective date.

rows.title: FAQ’s - Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated December 14, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/57) updates and republishes FAQs for all listed companies on filing the shareholding pattern under Regulation 31 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, specifically the disclosure of holding of specified securities and holding of specified securities in dematerialized form. The exchange states that the FAQs are based on past observations from shareholding pattern reports and are meant as guidance only, but companies are still expected to comply with the listing regulations and any other applicable regulations as amended from time to time.

A key requirement clarified for promoter/promoter group individuals is that if an individual promoter or promoter group member dies and their shares have not yet been transmitted to legal heirs by quarter-end, the company must continue to show the deceased person’s name in the promoter/promoter group section of the shareholding pattern and add detailed explanatory notes. Once transmission is completed, the deceased individual’s name may be removed from future shareholding pattern filings, but the legal heir’s name must be included and the company must again provide a detailed note describing the transmission of shares. In other words, the disclosure must reflect the legal ownership status as of the reporting date, and pending transmission does not justify omitting the deceased holder from the filing.

The circular also addresses cases where a promoter/promoter group company has been wound up or dissolved after a merger or amalgamation. Although the provided text cuts off before the full answer, the document clearly indicates that the FAQ is meant to explain how such entities should be shown in the shareholding pattern when the original promoter entity no longer exists because of corporate restructuring, and companies should follow the clarified treatment in their filings with the stock exchange. More broadly, the circular imposes no new standalone filing form or numerical threshold, but it does require companies to align their quarterly shareholding pattern disclosures with the updated FAQ guidance and to include detailed notes wherever ownership changes are not yet fully reflected because of death, transmission, merger, amalgamation, or dissolution.

rows.title: Guidance note on inclusion of "object of the issue" in case of preferential issue and in Qualified institutions placement.
rows.summary:
NSE has issued guidance dated December 13, 2022 for all listed companies on how to disclose the “object of the issue” in documents for preferential issues and Qualified Institutions Placement (QIP) under SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018. This follows the SEBI amendment of November 21, 2022, which requires appointment of a SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agency as the monitoring agency for utilization of issue proceeds when the issue size of a QIP or preferential issue exceeds ₹100 crore.  

The main compliance change is not a new approval requirement, but a disclosure standard meant to make issue proceeds easier to monitor: issuers must present the purpose of the fund-raising under a separate heading titled exactly “Object of the issue,” and they must state each object clearly rather than using open-ended or vague descriptions. For each object, the amount proposed to be used must be specified clearly; where the exact amount cannot be quantified, only a broad range may be given, and that range must be reasonable/narrow enough to identify the intended use.  

These instructions apply to the placement document for QIPs and the explanatory statement in the notice to shareholders for preferential issues. The practical effect is that any issuer undertaking these transactions should ensure its drafting is uniform and specific enough to allow the CRA monitoring agency to track actual use of proceeds against the stated objects.

rows.title: Circular for Seeking of comments, feedback on the XBRL for Regulation 30- OTS, ICA, Agreements, Fraud and Default
rows.summary:
NSE has issued a consultation circular dated **November 22, 2022** (Ref. **NSE/CML/2022/55**) to **all listed companies** seeking comments and feedback on a proposal to move certain **Regulation 30 disclosures** from **PDF to XBRL format** for stock exchange submissions. The proposed XBRL migration would apply specifically to announcements relating to **one-time settlements (OTS) / Inter-Creditors Agreements**, **agreements that are binding and not in the ordinary course of business, including any revisions, amendments, or terminations of those agreements**, and **fraud/default disclosures involving a promoter, key managerial personnel, the listed entity, or arrest of a promoter or key managerial personnel**.

The circular explains that this is part of the ongoing effort to standardize securities market data and follows the broader trend that listed entities have already been required to make **XBRL-based financial filings since 2015**. It states that stock exchanges have been working in phases to convert filings under SEBI regulations from PDF into XBRL, and that the current proposal is to extend that standardization to these Regulation 30 disclosure categories, as required under the **SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015**, read with the **SEBI circular dated September 9, 2015**, as amended.

This document is **not yet a final implementation notice** imposing the new filing method; its stated purpose is to **collect comments/feedback on the proposal**. Compliance teams should therefore treat it as an advance indication that these disclosure types may soon require structured XBRL submissions instead of narrative PDF attachments, and should be prepared for future procedural changes in how these announcements are drafted, tagged, and filed once the proposal is finalized.

The circular does not provide a new mandatory effective date, transition timeline, filing deadline, or technical schema in the excerpt provided, but it clearly signals the affected reporting population: **all listed companies** that make Regulation 30 announcements covering the specified OTS, agreement, fraud, default, and arrest events.

rows.title: : Master Circular on issuance of No Objection Certificate (NOC) for release of 1% of Issue Amount
rows.summary:
SEBI has issued a master circular dated **November 7, 2022** titled **“Master Circular on issuance of No Objection Certificate (NOC) for release of 1% of Issue Amount,”** and the National Stock Exchange circulated it to **all companies whose securities are listed on SEBI-recognized stock exchanges** on **November 9, 2022** for information and necessary action. The NSE notice itself does not restate the substantive procedure in detail; it serves to notify listed issuers that the updated SEBI circular is now the governing reference for obtaining an NOC to release **1% of the issue amount**.

For compliance purposes, the key point is that this communication applies to **listed companies/issuers** that are subject to SEBI and exchange listing requirements and may seek or need an NOC in connection with the release of the specified **1% of issue amount**. The document directs companies to the circular posted on the NSE website for the operative instructions, implying that any internal compliance or issue-management process should be aligned to the updated SEBI framework in force from **November 7, 2022**. No additional thresholds, timelines, filing steps, or exemptions are specified in the NSE notice itself beyond the reference to the **1% issue amount** and the instruction to take “necessary action.”

rows.title: Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds
rows.summary:
This notice is a forwarding communication from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to all Asset Management Companies (AMCs), advising them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/DOF2/P/CIR/2022/145 dated October 28, 2022, titled “Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds.” The document does not itself announce any new substantive requirement, threshold, procedure, or deadline; it simply references the SEBI circular and states that a copy is available on the NSE website for information and reference.  

For compliance purposes, the only directly affected entities identified here are AMCs, but the notice is informational rather than operative. No implementation date, compliance timeline, reporting obligation, or operational change is described in this text beyond the existence of the underlying SEBI circular dated October 28, 2022.

rows.title: Corrigendum on Standard Operating Process under SEBI (PIT) Regulations, 2015 for ensuring compliance with Structured Digital Database (SDD)
rows.summary:
The NSE issued a corrigendum dated November 4, 2022, to its earlier circular of October 28, 2022 regarding the Standard Operating Process under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 for compliance with the Structured Digital Database (SDD) requirement. The key requirement is that listed companies must comply with Regulation 3(5) and 3(6) of the SEBI PIT Regulations, which require the company to maintain an SDD; the circular applies to all listed companies on the NSE, including equity and/or debt listed entities.

The practical enforcement point is that if a company is not compliant with the SDD requirements, the Exchange will mark the company as non-compliant on the “Get Quote” page of the Exchange website. This non-compliance display will begin from the next trading day and will remain visible until the Exchange has satisfactorily verified that the company has fully complied with the SDD requirements.

For compliance teams, the immediate obligation is to confirm that the company has a compliant SDD in place and can evidence complete compliance with Reg. 3(5) and 3(6), since the Exchange may publicly flag deficiencies on its website. No monetary penalties, numerical thresholds, or additional deadlines are specified in this corrigendum beyond the “next trading day” publication trigger and continuation until verification of full compliance.

rows.title: Seeking of comments / feedback on the XBRL being introduced for submission of Announcements pertaining to Outcome of Board Meeting (Dividend, Buyback, Bonus shares and Voluntary Delisting)
rows.summary:
This document is a request for comments/feedback from listed entities on a new XBRL-based filing requirement for announcements relating to the outcome of a Board Meeting, specifically where the board approves or recommends a **dividend, buyback, bonus issue, or voluntary delisting**. In substance, the regulator is signaling that these board-outcome disclosures will no longer be submitted only as free-form announcements; instead, they will be converted into a structured **XBRL reporting format** so that listed entities must populate the relevant fields in the prescribed taxonomy when making these announcements.

For compliance purposes, the key change is the move from narrative-only disclosure to a standardized, machine-readable submission for these particular corporate actions. That means the affected listed entities will need internal processes to capture and validate the exact transaction details at the time of board approval—such as the dividend amount/rate, buyback size and terms, bonus ratio, or delisting details—because those inputs will likely have to be mapped to specific XBRL fields rather than stated loosely in a press release. The document is explicitly seeking market feedback before final implementation, so it is not itself the final operational instruction, but it is a clear indication that the reporting method is being formalized and that affected issuers should prepare for additional filing discipline and data-quality controls.

No specific effective date, transition deadline, numerical threshold, or exemption is visible in the provided text excerpt. Based on the title and visible content, the affected activities are announcements of board-meeting outcomes in relation to **dividend, buyback, bonus shares, and voluntary delisting**, and the compliance implication is that issuers handling these actions should monitor the final circular and be ready to update disclosure workflows, approval checklists, and filing ownership so the XBRL submission can be completed accurately and on time once the requirement is adopted.

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT
rows.summary: This notice is a forwarding circular from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to listed companies, informing them of a SEBI circular dated September 28, 2022, titled “Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT.” The exchange states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action,” but the text provided here does not itself set out the substantive amendments, the underlying compliance conditions, or any detailed procedures. The affected parties are listed companies, specifically those that are or may be involved with a listed REIT’s preferential issue or institutional placement of units. The only dated item in the notice is the SEBI circular itself, issued on September 28, 2022; no separate implementation deadline, threshold, rate, or filing date is stated in the covering communication. From a compliance perspective, the key action is to review the enclosed SEBI circular directly and assess whether any REIT-related issuance or placement activity needs to be adjusted to comply with the amended guidelines.

rows.title: XBRL based filing of Shareholding Pattern Report for Listed Companies at NSE
rows.summary:
This NSE circular requires all listed companies to file the Shareholding Pattern Report in XBRL mode through the NEAPS portal, in line with SEBI circular SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/92 dated June 30, 2022 on disclosure of holdings of specified securities and holdings of specified securities in dematerialized form. NSE states that the Excel Utility for preparing the Shareholding Pattern Report in the prescribed XBRL format will be available from **October 1, 2022** at **NEAPS > Compliance > Periodic Compliances > Share Holding Pattern > SHP Submission > Download SHP XBRL Utility**.

For submission, companies must use the XBRL utility to generate an **XML file**, then upload it on NEAPS via **NEAPS > Compliance > Common XBRL Upload > select “Shareholding Pattern” from the dropdown > Upload XBRL File > browse and select the XML file**. After a successful upload, the system will display **“File Uploaded successfully.”** The circular also points companies to the **June 30, 2022 NSE circular FAQs** regarding the new shareholder categories/subcategories introduced by the SEBI circular, but makes clear those FAQs are for **guidance only** and do not replace the legal filing requirements.

The practical compliance obligation is that listed entities must ensure their shareholding pattern disclosures are prepared and submitted in the new XBRL-based format and remain compliant with the **Listing Regulations and any other applicable regulations, as amended from time to time**. If companies have questions or technical issues, NSE directs them to email **nsexbrl@nse.co.in** or call the toll-free number **1800 266 0050 (IVR option 4)**.

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT
rows.summary:
The notice is an NSE cover letter informing all listed companies of a SEBI circular dated September 28, 2022, titled **“Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT.”** The letter itself does **not** set out the substantive rule changes; it only states that the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action” and is being circulated for information. From a compliance standpoint, the document indicates that **listed InvIT-related issuances** are the subject of the amended guidelines, so any entity involved in a **listed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)**—particularly those considering a **preferential issue** or **institutional placement of units**—should review the SEBI circular directly to determine the amended procedural and disclosure requirements.

No effective date, deadline, numerical threshold, pricing formula, approval requirement, or filing timeline is provided in the text of the NSE cover letter. The only date stated is the SEBI circular date itself, **September 28, 2022**. For compliance purposes, this letter should be treated as a transmission notice pointing recipients to a regulatory amendment affecting InvIT fundraising mechanics, but it does not by itself impose a standalone obligation beyond reviewing and acting on the enclosed SEBI circular.

rows.title: Revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on application filed under Regulation 37 of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 w.r.t. Scheme of Arrangements
rows.summary:
The circular revises the Standard Operating Procedure for listed entities seeking stock exchange NOC under Regulation 37 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 for a scheme of arrangement. It applies to all listed companies submitting draft schemes of arrangement to the exchanges, and it ties the process to the SEBI LODR framework, SEBI’s March 10, 2017 circular as amended, SEBI’s Master Circular dated November 23, 2021, and NSE circular NSE/CML/2021/43 dated November 2, 2021.

The key procedural change is that the scheme application, together with all documents required under the Exchange Checklist, must be filed with the exchange within 15 working days of the board meeting approving the draft scheme. If the company misses that 15-working-day window, it cannot proceed on the earlier board approval and must obtain fresh board approval based on updated materials, specifically including fresh financials, a fresh valuation report, and related current information.

For schemes involving one or more unlisted companies, the filing must include audited financial statements for the last 3 years, and those financials must not be older than 6 months at the time of submission. These statements are required under para I(A)(2)(f) of the SEBI circular dated March 10, 2017, as amended, read with the November 23, 2021 Master Circular, and they are specifically to be used by the valuer in preparing the valuation report under the Income Approach. This means listed entities must ensure the valuation exercise is based on recently prepared audited financials, not stale data.

The circular also adds a compliance undertaking requirement at the observation-letter stage: when the stock exchange issues its observation letter, it will require the listed entity to provide an undertaking confirming that it will ensure the financials used for the scheme remain current and compliant with the applicable SEBI requirements. In practical terms, compliance teams should treat this as a filing-timing control and a documentation-control update: delay beyond 15 working days triggers a reset of board approval, and unlisted-entity financials must be audited, cover three years, and be within the 6-month freshness limit at submission.

rows.title: Framework on Social Stock Exchange
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is informational and does not itself impose new obligations, but it alerts all social enterprises and all listed companies to SEBI’s detailed Social Stock Exchange (SSE) framework issued on September 19, 2022. The background change is that SEBI had already amended the ICDR Regulations, LODR Regulations, and AIF Regulations by notification dated July 25, 2022 to create the broad legal framework for SSEs, and the September 19 circular provides the operative details of that framework.

For compliance teams, the key point is that the SSE framework is intended to govern how eligible social enterprises can access capital and how such activity will be regulated through the exchange ecosystem. The circular does not, in this NSE cover note, specify the detailed eligibility criteria, filing steps, disclosure formats, or ongoing compliance requirements; it simply states that SEBI has now issued the detailed circular and encloses it for reference. No effective date, filing deadline, threshold, or rate is stated in the NSE note itself, so any actionable compliance obligations would need to be taken from the enclosed SEBI circular and the referenced amended regulations.

From a corporate compliance perspective, the notice means affected entities should review whether they qualify or intend to participate as a “social enterprise” on the SSE, and listed companies should monitor whether any of their disclosures, fundraising plans, or exchange-related obligations are impacted by the new framework. Because the NSE communication is only an informational forwarding note, it does not create a standalone submission requirement or deadline on its own.

rows.title: Guidance note on use of digital signature certificate for announcements submitted by listed companies
rows.summary:
NSE Circular NSE/CML/2022/44 dated September 7, 2022 provides a guidance note on the prior circular NSE/CML/2022/39 dated August 2, 2022, which required listed entities to authenticate filings and documents submitted to the stock exchange using a digital signature certificate (DSC). The guidance note is expressly for reference only, but it clarifies that the DSC requirement applies to all listed entities on NSE and, as a general rule, covers all corporate announcements/submissions made to the exchange.

The note confirms that, at present, all corporate announcements must be submitted using DSC except for specified exclusions already identified in the circular. From the text provided, those exclusions include: an outcome of a board meeting that includes only financial results, and disclosures where the relevant documents are issued by other entities (the excerpt cuts off after this point, so the full list of exclusions may continue in the referenced circular). This means compliance teams should treat DSC authentication as the default filing method for listed-company announcements unless the submission clearly falls within a stated exception.

The guidance note is issued alongside and should be read with NSE Circular NSE/CML/2018/02 dated January 16, 2018 and NSE/CML/2018/03 dated January 17, 2018, which are attached for reference. No new effective date, numerical threshold, or rate is introduced in the guidance note itself; rather, it clarifies implementation of the earlier DSC requirement for listed-company announcements submitted to NSE. For compliance purposes, the practical obligation is to ensure that all covered corporate announcements are digitally signed before submission, and to verify whether any filing qualifies for an express exception under the applicable NSE circulars.

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT
rows.summary:
The document is a cover letter from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies, informing them of SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/0116 dated August 26, 2022, titled “Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed REIT.” The letter itself does not set out the full amended rules; instead, it advises recipients that SEBI has issued revised guidelines governing preferential issues and institutional placements by listed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and encloses the SEBI circular for reference and necessary action. No specific compliance deadline, numerical threshold, or procedural change is described in the cover letter itself, and no immediate obligation is stated beyond reviewing the enclosed SEBI circular and taking action as applicable.

For a compliance team, the key takeaway from this document is that it is a notice of regulatory change affecting listed REIT capital-raising activities, not a substantive rule summary. The affected entities are listed REITs and the market participants involved in preferential allotments or institutional placements of REIT units; however, the exact amendments, conditions, and operational requirements are contained in the referenced SEBI circular rather than in this letter.

rows.title: Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT
rows.summary:
This communication is a transmittal notice from the National Stock Exchange of India Limited to listed companies, informing them of an SEBI circular dated **August 26, 2022**: **SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/0115**, titled **“Amendments to guidelines for preferential issue and institutional placement of units by a listed InvIT.”** The letter itself does **not** set out the substantive rule changes, thresholds, procedures, or compliance steps; it only says the SEBI circular is enclosed for reference and “necessary action” and that the notice is for information.

For a compliance team, the only directly stated action is to review the enclosed SEBI circular because it contains the operative amendments applicable to **listed InvITs** and their **preferential issue** and **institutional placement** of units. No effective date, implementation deadline, numerical threshold, or procedural requirement is provided in the body of this notice beyond the circular’s issuance date of **August 26, 2022**. If you need a substantive compliance summary, the actual SEBI circular text would be required, because this document is only a cover/intimation letter.

rows.title: Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds
rows.summary:
This document is not itself a substantive regulatory amendment; it is an NSE communication addressed to all Asset Management Companies (AMCs) simply pointing readers to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/DF2/CIR/P/2022/102 dated July 28, 2022, titled “Addendum to SEBI Circular on Development of Passive Funds.” The notice states that a copy of the SEBI circular is available on the NSE website for reference and expressly says the communication is “for your information,” without setting out any new obligations, procedures, deadlines, thresholds, or compliance changes in the text provided.

For compliance purposes, the only action implied by this notice is to review the referenced SEBI circular itself, since that separate circular may contain the actual requirements applicable to AMCs and passive fund development. Based on the text here alone, there are no new reporting requirements, operational steps, effective dates, or entity-specific obligations introduced by the NSE notice beyond awareness of the referenced SEBI circular.

rows.title: Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **August 5, 2022** does not itself create the substantive rule; it forwards and draws attention to the underlying **SEBI circular of the same date** titled **“Trading Window closure period under Clause 4 of Schedule B read with Regulation 9 of the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015 (“PIT Regulations”) – Framework for restricting trading by Designated Persons (“DPs”) by freezing PAN at security level.”** The key point for compliance teams is that SEBI has introduced a **framework to restrict trading by Designated Persons by freezing the PAN at the security level**, meaning trading limitations are to be implemented in a way that blocks transactions in the relevant securities for PANs associated with DPs during trading window closure periods.

The document is addressed to **all listed companies** and instructs them to take the enclosed SEBI circular into account for **necessary action at their end**. No separate implementation date, deadline, numeric threshold, or rate is stated in the NSE covering circular itself; the operative date referenced is **August 5, 2022**, which is also the date of the SEBI circular being circulated. Compliance teams should therefore review the SEBI circular and ensure their insider trading controls, trading window closure procedures, and broker/exchange-facing restrictions can support **PAN-level freezing for affected securities** in line with the PIT Regulations.

In practical terms, this means listed companies should verify that their designated-person monitoring and trade-restriction processes are aligned with the new SEBI mechanism, rather than relying only on manual communication of the trading window closure. The notice is informational from NSE, but it signals that the underlying SEBI requirement is the relevant compliance action item for listed entities and their insider-trading controls.

rows.title: Circular on use of digital signature certificate for announcements submitted by listed companies
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, issued by the Listing Department on August 2, 2022 (Ref. No. NSE/CML/2022/39), requires all listed companies to use a digital signature certificate when submitting announcements to the Stock Exchange through the electronic filing platforms NEAPS and the Digital Portal. The change is made in the context of Regulation 10 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, which already requires listed companies to file reports, statements, documents, filings, and other information electronically with the recognized stock exchange; the Exchange had previously provided user IDs and passwords for access, and SEBI had temporarily permitted digital signature-based authentication during COVID-19 through circulars dated April 17, 2020, July 31, 2020, and April 29, 2021.

Going forward, the Exchange, in consultation with other stock exchanges and SEBI, has decided to make digital signature certification mandatory for filing announcements under various SEBI regulations. This is a compliance requirement for listed companies submitting disclosures to the Exchange, and companies should ensure that the person making the filing uses a valid digital signature certificate for authentication/certification of the submission.

The circular carves out two specific exceptions where digital signature certification is not required: first, an announcement relating only to the outcome of a Board meeting that contains only financial results; and second, any disclosure that includes document(s) issued by entities other than the listed company itself, such as an auditor’s certificate or similar third-party documentation. The document does not specify a later effective date or transition period in the provided text, so the requirement should be treated as applicable from the circular date unless the Exchange separately provided implementation instructions.

rows.title: Guidance note on disclosures pertaining to analysts / institutional investors meet and best practices
rows.summary:
This NSE circular dated **July 29, 2022** (Ref. **NSE/CML/2022/38**) is addressed to **all listed companies** and serves as a **guidance note** on disclosures relating to **analyst / institutional investor meetings and conference calls** under **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**, specifically **point 15 of Part A of Schedule III**. It states that NSE had already issued an earlier guidance note on the same topic on **June 29, 2021** (circular **NSE/CML/2021/24**) and that this new note is a continuation intended to further clarify existing requirements and highlight industry best practices for reporting such meetings/calls. The document emphasizes that listed entities should **proactively disclose material information** through these meetings/calls in a way that supports investor decision-making and stakeholder trust, and reminds companies to comply not only with the LODR Regulations but also with **all other applicable regulations as amended from time to time**.

The guidance note is meant as a **benchmarking/reference document only**, not a separate mandatory rulebook, but it reiterates that disclosures are required **at various stages** of an analyst/institutional investor meet or call. The excerpt provided begins the first stage, **“Prior to the meet / call,”** stating that listed companies are required to **submit the schedule of analyst or institutional investor meetings/calls to the exchange in advance**. The document indicates that the guidance note is structured by disclosure stage for ease of understanding, and the underlying compliance expectation is that companies should follow the existing disclosure obligations under the listing regulations while adopting the described best practices for timely, complete, and transparent reporting.

rows.title: Levy of Goods and Services Tax (GST) on the fees payable to SEBI
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India, by circular NSE/CML/2022/37 dated July 20, 2022, informed all listed companies that SEBI had issued Circular No. SEBI/HO/GSD/TAD/CIR/P/2022/0097 dated July 18, 2022 on the “Levy of Goods & Services Tax (GST) on the fees payable to SEBI.” The NSE circular itself does not set out the detailed tax treatment or any operational instructions, but it expressly directs listed companies to note the SEBI circular and take “necessary action” as applicable. In practical terms, the compliance relevance is that fees payable to SEBI are now subject to GST under the referenced SEBI circular, so listed entities should review their SEBI fee payment processes, invoicing/tax accounting, and internal controls to ensure GST is correctly applied and paid where required.

The NSE communication is informational and does not specify a separate implementation date beyond the date of the SEBI circular (July 18, 2022) and the NSE forwarding date (July 20, 2022). No thresholds, rates, exemptions, or entity-specific carveouts are stated in the NSE text provided. Compliance teams should therefore rely on the underlying SEBI circular for the substantive GST mechanics and ensure the company’s finance/compliance functions incorporate that SEBI direction into payment and reporting procedures.

rows.title: Extension of time for filing of information required under Regulation 46 and 62 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 in NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System).
rows.summary:
This NSE circular extends the compliance deadline for listed entities to file the information required under Regulations 46 and 62 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 through the NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System). It follows NSE circular NSE/CML/2022/35 dated July 11, 2022, which announced the launch of the new NEAPS module for such filings.  

The substantive change is that, instead of filing by the earlier timeline tied to the module release, listed entities were granted additional time to complete these Regulation 46 and 62 disclosures, with the extended deadline set at **August 31, 2022**. The circular states that this extension was granted after receiving representations from listed entities and considering the practical difficulties they faced in adapting to the new filing process.  

The requirement applies to **all listed entities** on the NSE that must submit information under **Regulation 46 and Regulation 62** of the SEBI Listing Regulations via NEAPS. No new thresholds, rates, or additional substantive disclosure items are introduced in this circular; the key compliance obligation is simply to ensure the required filings are completed in NEAPS by the new extended date. For clarifications, the exchange provides contact persons **Mr. Aniket Raut (araut@nse.co.in)** and **Ms. Dhwani Shah (cdfr_dshah@nse.co.in)**.

rows.title: Release of new module for filing of information required under Regulation 46 and 62 of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 on NEAPS (NSE Electronic Application Processing System)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) issued a circular on July 11, 2022, introducing a new NEAPS module for compliance with Regulations 46 and 62 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, which require listed entities to maintain a functional website containing specified basic company information. Under this circular, **all listed entities** must now upload the **URLs of the information required under Regulations 46 and 62** through NEAPS, using the designated path for the initial filing: **NEAPS > Periodic Compliance > Regulation for Functional Website**. If any of the posted information changes later, the listed entity must update it through the modification path: **NEAPS > Reports > Regulation for Functional Website**. The filing obligation was to be completed **by July 18, 2022**, and the circular specifically directs all listed entities to take note and ensure the required submission by that date.

From a compliance perspective, this means companies must verify that their website disclosures covered by Regulations 46 and 62 are accessible and that the relevant web links are accurately captured in NEAPS. The circular does not introduce a new substantive website-disclosure standard, but it adds a mandatory **NSE reporting step** for the required website information and imposes an explicit deadline for initial compliance. For questions, the NSE provided contact points: **Mr. Aniket Raut (araut@nse.co.in)** and **Ms. Dhwani Shah (cdfr_dshah@nse.co.in)**.

rows.title: Release of New Digital Portal for filing of Information with the Exchange - for Financial results, Related Party Transactions (RPT) and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) announced, by Circular NSE/CML/2022/34 dated July 8, 2022, an expansion of its new Digital Portal for listed-company filings under the SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015. This circular continues the earlier portal rollout under NSE/CML/2022/03 (January 6, 2022) and follows the separate July 8, 2022 circular NSE/CML/2022/18 on digital filings for equity announcements/disclosures under SEBI takeover regulations.  

For **all NSE-listed entities**, the following filings must be submitted on the **new Digital Portal beginning July 11, 2022** as part of **phase 2**: **Financial Results XBRL submission** (path: Digital Exchange > Compliance > Financial Results > Full Results), **Related Party Transactions (RPT) XBRL submission** (Digital Exchange > Compliance > Financial Results > Related Party Transactions), and **Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR) XBRL submission** (Digital Exchange > Compliance > Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report (BRSR)). The circular does not change the underlying SEBI disclosure content itself, but it changes the **filing channel** for these items from the existing process to the new portal as of that date.  

All **other filings** are to continue through the **existing NEAPS portal** unless and until NSE migrates them later. NSE also stated that it will separately share details of a **demo/training session** on how to use the new portal for these disclosures. For operational support, NSE set up a dedicated help desk with toll-free number **1800 266 0050 (IVR option 4)** and email **compliancecustomersupport@nse.co.in**.

rows.title: Guidance Note on Regulation 13(3) of SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015 - Investor Complaints Report
rows.summary:
This guidance note reiterates the existing requirement under Regulation 13(3) of SEBI’s LODR Regulations, 2015 that every listed entity must file a quarterly investor complaints statement with the recognized stock exchange(s) within 21 days from the end of each quarter. The statement must report the number of complaints pending at the start of the quarter, received during the quarter, disposed of during the quarter, and remaining unresolved at quarter-end.

The main clarification in this circular is that companies must count **all** investor complaints received from **all sources**, not just those routed through SEBI SCORES or the stock exchange. The document specifically says complaints received directly by the company through email, letters/hard copies, or other channels to officials handling investor grievances must also be included in the quarterly report. In other words, the company’s reported totals must reconcile to the full universe of complaints received, whether through SCORES, the exchange, or directly.

The circular gives an example to show how the calculation should work: if a listed company receives 5 complaints through SCORES, 5 through the exchange, and 5 directly by email/letter, then total complaints received for the quarter are 15. If 3 SCORES complaints, 2 exchange complaints, and all 5 directly received complaints are resolved during the quarter, then 10 are disposed of and 5 remain pending at quarter-end. The circular notes that if the numbers disclosed in the quarterly Investor Complaint(s) Report do not match the complaints actually received from all sources, the exchange may initiate action against the company.

For compliance purposes, the practical obligation is to maintain a consolidated complaint-tracking process that captures every investor grievance received by the company, regardless of source, and ensures the quarterly filing is complete and internally consistent with SCORES and exchange-forwarded complaints. The guidance note is dated July 7, 2022 (NSE/CML/2022/33) and is addressed to the Company Secretary of all listed companies.

rows.title: Advisory under Regulation 46 and 62 of SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure Requirements) Regulation, 2015
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, dated **July 04, 2022** and addressed to **all listed entities**, reiterates existing obligations under **SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015**—specifically **Regulation 46** for equity-listed entities and **Regulation 62** for debt-listed entities—requiring each listed company to maintain a **functional website** with basic company information and the required regulatory disclosures. The circular does **not create new substantive disclosure requirements**, but it directs listed entities to reorganize how those disclosures are presented on their websites so they are placed in a **separate, clearly identifiable section** and are easier to locate, rather than being scattered across the site.

For **Regulation 46(2)** disclosures, the website should include a dedicated path such as **Home > Investors > Disclosures under Regulation 46 of the LODR**, containing the items required under that sub-regulation. For **Regulation 62(1)** disclosures, the website should similarly use a dedicated path such as **Home > Investors > Disclosures under Regulation 62 of the LODR**, containing the disclosures required for debt-listed entities. The circular also flags a common deficiency: many companies upload policies without showing when they were last changed, so listed entities are now advised to ensure that every policy uploaded to the website is updated with its **effective date or last amended date**.

There is **no specific compliance deadline** stated in the circular, but it instructs listed entities to **take necessary steps immediately** to align with these expectations and remain compliant with the cited Listing Regulations. In practical terms, compliance teams should verify that the website has proper indexing, all required disclosures are consolidated in the prescribed investor/disclosure sections, and all published policies display a date showing either when they became effective or when they were last amended.

rows.title: FAQ's - Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India issued this circular on **June 30, 2022** to all listed companies, forwarding SEBI’s circular **SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/92 dated June 30, 2022** on **disclosure of holding of specified securities and holding of specified securities in dematerialized form**. The circular does not create a new standalone rule in itself; rather, it provides **FAQs for guidance** on the **new shareholder categories/sub-categories** introduced by the SEBI framework, and it reminds companies that they must comply with the **Listing Regulations and all other applicable regulations, as amended from time to time**.

A key clarification is that a shareholder **must not be disclosed twice** in the shareholding pattern. If a holder has already been reported in **Table II (Statement showing shareholding pattern of the Promoter and Promoter Group)**, that same holder **should not be repeated in Table III (Statement showing shareholding pattern of the Public shareholder)**; put differently, anyone who qualifies as a **“promoter” or “promoter group”** holder is excluded from public-shareholder disclosure in Table III. The FAQs also state that if a shareholder fits **more than one category in Table III**, the company must classify and disclose that holder **in the category that appears first in the prescribed order of the shareholding pattern format**.

For compliance purposes, the practical obligation is to ensure that the shareholding pattern is prepared **consistently with the order and definitions in the prescribed format**, avoiding duplication between promoter/promoter-group and public-shareholder tables and using the prescribed priority order where categories overlap. The exchange notes that the FAQs are **only guidance** and should be read alongside the underlying SEBI circular and applicable listing and securities law requirements.

rows.title: Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form
rows.summary:
This NSE circular is a forwarding notice to **all listed companies** from the **Company Secretary** function, informing them of a new **SEBI circular dated June 30, 2022** on **“Disclosure of holding of specified securities and Holding of specified securities in dematerialized form.”** The NSE circular itself does **not** set out new substantive requirements; rather, it states that the SEBI circular is enclosed and should be reviewed for **necessary action**, and notes that the same circular is also available on the NSE website.

From a compliance perspective, the key point is that listed companies are being directed to take note of—and act on—the **SEBI-issued requirements** regarding disclosure of holdings of specified securities and the reporting/maintenance of holdings in **dematerialized form**. The circular is dated **June 30, 2022** and references **SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2022/92**. No effective date, deadline, thresholds, rates, or detailed procedural changes are specified in the NSE cover letter itself; those would need to be obtained from the enclosed SEBI circular.

rows.title: Reduction of timelines for listing of units of privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)
rows.summary:
The National Stock Exchange of India is circulating SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/DDHS/DDHS_Div3/P/CIR/2022/087 dated June 24, 2022, titled **“Reduction of timelines for listing of units of privately placed Infrastructure Investment Trust (InvIT)”**. The NSE notice itself does not set out the substantive rule changes, but it expressly directs listed companies to refer to the enclosed SEBI circular and take any necessary action. In other words, the operative regulatory change comes from SEBI’s June 24, 2022 circular, and the NSE communication is a forwarding notice to all listed companies.

For compliance purposes, the key point in this document is that it concerns the **timelines for listing units of privately placed InvITs** and indicates that those timelines have been reduced. The document does not provide the new timeline, the prior timeline, or any numerical deadlines in the text shown here, so a compliance team would need to review the attached SEBI circular for the exact compliance date and procedural requirements. The NSE letter is dated **June 28, 2022** and is addressed to **the Company Secretary / all listed companies**, making it relevant as a regulatory update to be tracked, even if a company is only indirectly affected.

No filing instruction, reporting threshold, or company-specific obligation is stated in the NSE notice itself beyond acknowledging receipt and action on the enclosed SEBI circular. A compliance officer should therefore treat this as a prompt to review whether the organization has any exposure to InvIT issuance, listing, trustee/sponsor activity, or related market-facing obligations, and to update internal timelines and controls if the SEBI circular changes listing deadlines for privately placed InvIT units.

rows.title: Filing of Report to SEBI in respect of any acquisition made in reliance upon exemption provided for in regulation 10 of SEBI (SAST) Regulations, 2011
rows.summary:
The NSE has clarified the filing procedure for reports to SEBI under Regulation 10(7) of the SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011, which applies where an acquisition is made in reliance on an exemption under Regulation 10. Effective from the date of this circular, such reports are no longer to be filed through general means; instead, acquirers and listed entities must submit them to SEBI **only by email** to the dedicated address **sastexemptionapplication@sebi.gov.in**. The email submission must include the **details of the fees paid** along with the report.  

This requirement affects **acquirers** relying on a Regulation 10 exemption and **all listed companies** that may be involved in or overseeing such filings, and the circular instructs listed companies to take note and ensure compliance accordingly. The document does not specify a separate compliance deadline or transition period; it is a procedural instruction that applies immediately to the filing of Regulation 10(7) reports.

rows.title: Guidance note for filing intimations w.r.t. Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) / Inter-Creditors Agreement (ICA)
rows.summary:
This NSE circular, effective as of June 7, 2022, instructs all listed companies and all Interim Resolution Professionals (IRPs) / Resolution Professionals (RPs) to file all Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) / Inter-Creditors Agreement (ICA) related disclosures only through the Exchange’s new digital portal, and to use the specifically designated announcement subjects for each stage of the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP). It reinforces prior Exchange circulars from September 24, 2019, July 9, 2021, and May 20, 2022, and states that the required intimations must be made strictly in the new portal rather than through other routes.

The circular gives the exact filing paths for the main CIRP milestones: for commencement/admission of CIRP, users must log in to `https://digitalexchange.nseindia.com` and navigate to `Compliance > Equity > New Announcement > Category: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process > Subject Type: CIRP – Commencement`; for approval of a resolution plan by the Hon’ble NCLT, the same route is used but with `Subject Type: CIRP – Approval of Resolution Plan`; and for withdrawal of CIRP by the Hon’ble NCLT, the same digital portal path is to be used under the corresponding withdrawal subject (the document indicates this as the required route for that event as well). The practical compliance obligation is that disclosure timing and categorization must match the relevant CIRP stage, with the announcement submitted under the correct subject type in the Exchange’s digital system.

The document also ties into the Exchange’s newer surveillance framework for securities under IBC/ICA, meaning the filing discipline is intended to support both regulatory disclosure and market surveillance.
